ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: talks about the early days
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: talks at meals about how the colony began

plain.li: I've started telling the newer ones how this place was when I came. Most of them have no idea how bare it was.
We talked about the first days the other evening, and now I keep remembering more of it.
[tribal] I tell the young ones how the camp was in the first winter, so they know what was done before them.
[spacer] I keep telling people how little we had when we first got here.

warm.li: I like remembering the early days out loud. It reminds me how far we've all come.

blunt.li: I talk about the early days now. People can listen or not.

cheerful.li: I've got a story about the early days for every meal. Nobody has stopped me yet.

gloomy.li: I keep thinking about the ones who were here at the start and aren't any more.

cold.li: The newer ones should know how the colony began, so I tell them.

plain.li: I didn't bring up the early days once this week. I think I've told every story I have.

warm.li: The newer ones know the old stories now. They tell them better than I do.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: looks out for newcomers
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: has a word for any newcomer nearby

plain.li: I remember what my first days here were like. Now when someone new comes, I make sure they have someone to ask.
Someone showed me how things work here when I was new. I'll do the same for the next one.
[child] When I was new, someone was nice to me. Now I'm nice to the new ones.
[tribal] When I came to this camp, someone made room for me at the fire. I do that for the new ones now.

warm.li: Nobody should feel like a stranger here for long. I keep an eye on the new ones.

blunt.li: New people need someone to ask. That's me now.

cheerful.li: I love it when someone new arrives. I get to show them everything.

gloomy.li: I know how lonely the first days are. I don't want anyone else to feel like that.

cold.li: Newcomers settle in faster with help. It's worth the time.

plain.li: The last newcomer found their own way without me. That's how it should be.

cheerful.li: Everyone here has settled in. There's nobody left for me to show round.

plain.li: Ever since that game I play to win, every time. A game isn't worth playing otherwise.
I keep the score in my head now, for every game and every race.
[child] I'm going to win the next game, I've decided.
[tribal] Whoever wins at the games gets talked about at the fire. I want to be the one they talk about.

warm.li: I play to win, but I shake hands afterwards. Mostly.

blunt.li: I don't like losing. So I don't.

cheerful.li: I've decided I'm going to win the next game, and the one after that.

gloomy.li: I lost that game and I can't stop thinking about it.

cold.li: Losing comes from not enough practice, so I practise.

plain.li: I lost a game yesterday and laughed about it. I must be getting over it.

cheerful.li: I played just for fun today and didn't keep score once.

plain.li: After we made up I felt so much better that I can't stand seeing anyone else stay angry. I tell them to sort it out.
A quarrel left alone only gets worse. I try to get people talking again.
[tribal] My people never let a quarrel go on overnight. I've started saying so to anyone who's sulking.

warm.li: It upsets me to see two people here not speaking. I do what I can.

blunt.li: If you two have a problem, talk to each other. I say that a lot now.

cheerful.li: I've become the one who makes everyone shake hands. I'm good at it.

gloomy.li: Every quarrel here worries me. There aren't enough of us to fall out.

cold.li: Grudges waste time and work, so I try to end them.

plain.li: Two people argued at the table and I let them get on with it. I've stopped trying to fix everything.

cold.li: People can settle their own quarrels. I've stopped stepping in.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: always has time for the children
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: has a word for any child nearby

plain.li: I've noticed how much the children want someone to talk to. I always stop for them now.
A child asked me something I couldn't answer quickly, so I sat down and answered it properly. I do that every time now.
[tribal] Children learn from whoever will talk to them. I make sure it's me.

warm.li: There's always time for the children. The work can wait a minute.

blunt.li: Children ask questions. I answer them.

cheerful.li: The children have worked out that I'll always stop and talk. I don't mind at all.

gloomy.li: They grow up so fast here. I want them to remember that someone had time for them.

cold.li: Children who get answers learn faster. It's time well spent.

plain.li: The children have stopped following me around with questions. They find their own answers now, mostly.

warm.li: The children don't need me as much these days. I still stop for them when they ask.

plain.li: I like being with the old ones. They know how everything works and they don't mind telling me.
I follow the old ones around now. They let me help, and they tell me how things used to be.
[tribal] The old ones know all the stories and all the ways of doing things. I go where they go.

warm.li: The old ones are kind to me. I want to stay near them.

blunt.li: The old ones know things. I'm learning them.

cheerful.li: I'm the old ones' helper now. They said so.

gloomy.li: The old ones won't be here forever, so I want to learn everything from them now.

cold.li: The old ones have done everything already. It's quicker to learn from them.

plain.li: I don't follow the old ones around as much any more. I've got my own things to do now.

cheerful.li: I know how to do lots of things now, so I don't need to ask the old ones every time.
